This hearing has been done through hybrid mode (physical and virtual hearing).

2. The present petition relates to a consignment of Areca nuts which have been seized by the Customs authorities under Section 110 of the Customs Act, 1962, on the ground that they are not fit for human consumption.
The Custom authorities have relied upon the test reports of Respondent No. 4 - Food Safety Standards Authority of India (hereinafter 'FSSAI') to hold back the said goods.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Since the Petitioner is incurring a huge cost for retaining the goods at the Customs authorities, the prayer of the Digitally Signed By:DINESH SINGH NAYAL Signing Date:09.04.2021 18:13:10 Petitioner is that the Petitioner may be permitted to re-export these goods to the supplier itself.

3. Mr. Harpreet Singh, ld. Counsel submits that re-export would be permissible in accordance with Vishwa Enterprise, Through Its ... vs Union Of India, Through Its Secretary, ... on 8 April, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81282387/
1 Section 51 of the Customs Act, 1962 and if the Petitioner applies for re-exportation/exportation of the products, the same would be considered and processed in accordance with law.

4. Considering the fact that the Petitioner now wishes to apply to the Customs authorities for re-exportation of the products, let an application be moved within a period of three days by the Petitioner before the Customs authorities.
The same shall be considered and disposed of within a period of two weeks.
If any Customs Duty has been paid by the Petitioner, and if the Petitioner is entitled to any refunds, the same shall also be processed and allowed in accordance with law.
The remedies of the Petitioner in respect of any decisions taken by the Customs authorities are left open.
5. The petition is disposed of in the above terms.
